summary:
The academic layer is not pedagogy; it is a chat wrapper with a study-themed UI on top.
The spaced-repetition engine is real FSRS v4.5 code (server/fsrs_scheduler.py) but the route never
persists or reloads stability/difficulty, so schedule_review always takes its new-card branch and
every card gets the same constant interval (measured: 10 consecutive 'Good' reviews through the route
signature return [4,4,4,...] days). Mastery is one click: rating>=3 sets state='mastered'
(routes_study_tools.py:120) and mastery% counts it, so a deck reads 100% mastered after one pass.
Quiz grading is doubly broken: the generated practice test is a dict {multiple_choice,short_answer}
but both the grader and the web player expect a list, so a real quiz yields zero questions; and when
a list IS passed the MCQ answer key is read from keys the generator never emits, leaving
correct_answer='' so the containment test `correct_answer in submitted` marks every answer correct
(measured: 2/2 wrong answers -> 100%). Underneath, the flagship 'do_it_for_me' direction writes the
student's complete assignment draft (draft.py:89) and then runs an AI-detector-evasion humanizer loop
plus CDP keystroke injection configured so an LMS integrity monitor cannot tell automation from a
person (launch_to_doc.py:80-87) - directly contradicting PRIVACY_POLICY.md:87. Canvas integration is
genuinely read-only and token-based, but a second Canvas route bypasses the SSRF guard while carrying
the student's Bearer token.

findings.title: Quiz grading marks every multiple-choice answer correct (score is always 100%)
findings.symptom: A student finishes a practice test answering every question wrong and the score screen says 100%. The 'Retry only wrong questions' button then has nothing to retry.
findings.root_cause:
grade_quiz resolves the answer key from keys the practice-test generator never emits.
study_tools.py:155-165 generates items shaped {"q","options","answer_index","explanation"}, but
routes_study_tools.py:197-203 reads only correct_answer|answer|definition|back, so correct_answer
becomes "". The comparison at routes_study_tools.py:209 is
`submitted == correct_answer or submitted in correct_answer or correct_answer in submitted`; with
correct_answer=="" the third clause is an empty string contained in any non-empty string, which is
always True. The `bool(submitted and ...)` guard only requires a non-empty submission.
evidence: server/routes_study_tools.py:196-209 - correct_answer built from {correct_answer,answer,definition,back}; `is_correct = bool(submitted and (submitted == correct_answer or submitted in correct_answer or correct_answer in submitted))`
server/study_tools.py:156-163 - generator returns {"q","options","answer_index","explanation"} (no correct_answer/answer/back key)
measured: reproduced the exact loop with two generated MCQ items, both answers wrong -> correct_count=2, percentage=100.0
server/tests/test_study_tools_v3.py:32-35,78-93 - the only grade_quiz test uses a legacy {front,back} deck, never the practice_test MCQ shape, so the suite stays green
findings.impact: The core 'practice test' value proposition is false. Students get confident confirmation of wrong answers; the missed-concept/adaptive-review features built on this score (web/src/components/IntelligenceView.jsx:256) run on fabricated data.

evidence: server/study_tools.py:158-163 - required JSON shape is an object with multiple_choice/short_answer
server/main.py:680-685 - _material_payload json.loads practice_test content back to a dict

findings.title: FSRS is never actually run - no spaced repetition, every interval is a constant 4-value lookup
findings.symptom: Every card is rescheduled identically regardless of history: Again=1 day, Hard=2, Good=4, Easy=16. No card is ever 'due today' and no UI shows a review queue.
findings.root_cause:
review_card calls `scheduler.schedule_review(rating=payload.rating)` with no
current_stability, current_difficulty or last_review_time (routes_study_tools.py:118).
fsrs_scheduler.schedule_review branches to the new-card path whenever any of those is None
(fsrs_scheduler.py:105), so the entire DSR update code (retrievability/next_difficulty/
next_stability_recall/next_stability_forget, fsrs_scheduler.py:45-83) is dead in production. There is
nowhere to persist the state anyway: StudyCardState has `difficulty` as a String(16) and no numeric
stability/difficulty columns (database.py:272-286). The client-supplied `difficulty` is stored
verbatim and never read by the scheduler (routes_study_tools.py:128,136).
evidence: server/routes_study_tools.py:118 - review_res = scheduler.schedule_review(rating=payload.rating) (no prior state passed)
server/fsrs_scheduler.py:105 - `if current_stability is None or current_difficulty is None or last_review_time is None:` -> initial-only branch
server/fsrs_scheduler.py:37-38 - new-card interval is w[rating-1]: 0.403 / 1.184 / 3.173 / 15.691 -> 1/2/4/16 days
server/database.py:279-280 - StudyCardState.difficulty is a String; no stability/difficulty-value float columns exist
measured: .venv/bin/python - 10 x schedule_review(rating=3) through the route signature -> [4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4]

measured: read-only sqlite PRAGMA table_info(study_card_states) on data/db/helpotron.db -> ['id','user_id','material_id','card_index','state','difficulty','due','lapses','last_practiced','created_at']
server/tests/test_osr_engines.py:20-36 - the only FSRS test supplies stability/difficulty/elapsed itself, so it exercises the class and never the route
findings.impact: The central claim ('Study Materials & Spaced Repetition', 'adaptive spaced repetition player', web/src/components/LibraryView.jsx:151,462) is false. The scheduler is a 4-row constant table; the 'FSRS v4.5 / OSR-007' header (fsrs_scheduler.py:1-9) misrepresents shipped behaviour.

findings.title: 'Mastery' is awarded on a single button press
findings.symptom: One pass through a deck pressing Good shows '100% mastered' and an empty learning queue.
findings.root_cause:
review_card sets `new_state = 'mastered' if payload.rating >= 3 else ...`
(routes_study_tools.py:120) with no interval, lapse or repetition threshold. Both mastery aggregations
then count that state: decks counts ('mastered','known','review') (routes_study_tools.py:75), mastery
counts ('mastered','known') (routes_study_tools.py:321).
evidence: server/routes_study_tools.py:120 - new_state = "mastered" if payload.rating >= 3 else ("known" if payload.rating == 2 else "learning")
server/routes_study_tools.py:75 - mastered_count = sum(... cs.state in ("mastered","known","review"))
server/routes_study_tools.py:321-323 - mastered counts ('mastered','known'); mastery_pct = mastered/total
server/tests/test_study_tools_v3.py:57-75 - the test asserts state=='mastered' after one rating-3 review and mastery_percentage==50.0, locking in the wrong behaviour
findings.impact: The most persuasive number on the study screen is unearned. It rewards clicking through once, the opposite of the retrieval-practice effect the UI invokes.

findings.title: Academic integrity: the product writes the assignment and runs a detector-evasion + human-typing-simulation pipeline, contradicting its own published policy
findings.symptom: 'do_it_for_me' returns a complete assignment draft written from the student's transcript in the student's own writing voice; 'Launch to Doc' then types it into Google Docs at 65 wpm with jitter, typos and false starts using trusted (non-synthetic) keystrokes.
findings.root_cause:
assignment_team._do_it_for_me calls draft.generate_draft with the user's stored
writing style and stores the result as the assignment draft (assignment_team.py:127-213).
draft.build_style_prompt instructs 'Write a complete draft that directly addresses the assignment
prompt' with 'Do not include any meta-commentary' (draft.py:76-91, echoed at 100-118). The draft then
runs through AIHumanizerPipeline.humanize_loop, whose module docstring is 'Multi-engine AI detection
evasion' (humanizer.py:1) and whose LLM pass says 'Transform the student's assignment draft to
eliminate all statistical AI markers' (humanizer.py:539-540), exposing an `is_stealth_ready` flag
(humanizer.py:567). draft._draft_workflow_async retries generation up to MAX_RETRIES=5 until the
detector suite passes (draft.py:31,225-293). launch_to_doc.TYPING_DEFAULTS sets trusted_keys=True
because 'that one property is what a page (and therefore an LMS integrity monitor) can read to tell
automation from a person' (launch_to_doc.py:75-87), with false_start_rate 0.025. PRIVACY_POLICY.md:87
states the opposite: 'The detector scoring shown in your dashboard is a transparency risk meter, not a
concealing tool.' No generation prompt requires citations or disclosure; study_tools._SYSTEM says only
'Be accurate to the transcript' and 'Never fabricate sources or quotes' (study_tools.py:36-43).
evidence: server/assignment_team.py:127-213 - _do_it_for_me produces and stores a full first draft on the assignment
server/draft.py:89 - 'Write a complete draft that directly addresses the assignment prompt. Do not include any meta-commentary.'
server/draft.py:73-91,121-139 - build_style_prompt embeds the student's writing sample and generate_draft uses it; server/assignment_team.py:156-172 passes the stored style in
server/humanizer.py:1 - docstring: 'Multi-engine AI detection evasion, Kimhons 38-pattern scrubbing...'
server/humanizer.py:539-540 - 'Transform the student's assignment draft to eliminate all statistical AI markers, robotic cadence, uniform sentence lengths, and banned slop.'
server/humanizer.py:562-578 - detector suite with threshold 100-self.threshold and an is_stealth_ready verdict
server/draft.py:225-293 - `for attempt in range(1, MAX_RETRIES + 1)` regenerating until detectors pass; MAX_RETRIES=5 (draft.py:31)
server/launch_to_doc.py:79-87 - trusted_keys=True 'on by default for the typing surface... what a page (and therefore an LMS integrity monitor) can read to tell automation from a person'
server/launch_to_doc.py:41-64 - cadence presets carry wpm and typo_rate (academic: 65 wpm, 0.018)
PRIVACY_POLICY.md:87 - 'Submitting unreviewed AI output ... is prohibited by our Terms of Service. The detector scoring shown in your dashboard is a transparency risk meter, not a concealing tool.'
findings.impact: Largest legal/ethical exposure with educational institutions. The code implements exactly the concealment the published policy disclaims, turning a policy statement into an admission. Detector-evasion plus trusted-keystroke simulation is evidence of intent in a misconduct proceeding (external research: Exeter - 'hiding it could be a breach of academic integrity'; Langara found humanizer tools defeat Turnitin's detector).

findings.title: Study-material prompts have no source grounding, no citations, no difficulty calibration and no hallucination exit
findings.symptom: A study guide or deck can state concepts the lecture never covered, with nothing distinguishing transcript fact from model invention.
findings.root_cause:
The generators are single-shot prompts with no retrieval and no citation contract.
The only grounding instruction is a generic system line (study_tools.py:36-43). 'Reading level' is
free client input defaulted silently to 'college-freshman' (study_tools.py:45-56). Nothing asks the
model to cite the student's material, quote a transcript span, or refuse when the transcript lacks the
answer; retries check JSON shape only, never content (study_tools.py:129-144,169-178). Answer keys are
model-authored and never verified. There is no difficulty parameter at all:
generate_flashcards takes only (transcript, count, reading_level) and generate_practice_test only
(transcript, mc_count, short_answer_count, reading_level) (study_tools.py:112-125,147-165).
evidence: server/study_tools.py:36-43 - _SYSTEM: only 'Be accurate to the transcript; when the transcript doesn't cover something, say so instead of inventing it. Never fabricate sources or quotes.'
server/study_tools.py:96-103 - study-guide prompt asks for key concepts/exam questions, no citation or source-span requirement
server/study_tools.py:119-125 - flashcard prompt asks only for q/a JSON, no grounding field
server/study_tools.py:155-165 - practice-test prompt asks for q/options/answer_index/explanation; answer keys are model-asserted, never checked
server/study_tools.py:45-56 - reading level normalised to a fixed list, default 'college-freshman'; no difficulty parameter
server/study_tools.py:129-144,169-178 - retries validate JSON shape only
server/study_tools.py:228-249 - generate_study_pack is a second thinner path with the same absence of grounding
findings.impact: A confidently wrong study guide is worse than none and nothing here would detect one. Students cannot tell which claims came from their lecture. The AI-tutor RCT (Kestin & Miller) attributes its gains to expert-authored solution content and step-by-step accuracy guardrails, none of which exist here.

findings.title: The draft_section agent action is a hardcoded stub that returns fake prose
findings.symptom: Any path executing the agent's 'draft_section' action returns one canned sentence instead of drafting: 'Drafted comprehensive academic {section} addressing all primary inquiry parameters with structured argumentation.'
findings.root_cause: The action handler builds a string literal and returns it without calling any model (overlord_agent.py:1274-1281). 'draft_section' is in ROUTINE_ACTION_TYPES (overlord_agent.py:70) and is a reachable advertised capability keyword (assignment_direction.py:84-90).

server/overlord_agent.py:70 - 'draft_section' in ROUTINE_ACTION_TYPES
server/assignment_direction.py:84-90 - 'outline'/'explain'/'notes' capability keywords can route here
findings.impact: Silent placeholder in shipped, charged code. A student acting on this output gets nothing and cannot see it was never generated.

findings.title: Study routes do not check material ownership (IDOR on decks, review, mastery)
findings.symptom: Any authenticated user can POST a review against, and read the mastery of, another user's study material id.
findings.root_cause:
list_study_decks filters on user_id/shared_with (routes_study_tools.py:43-54), but
review_card, grade_quiz and get_deck_mastery fetch with `.filter(StudyMaterial.id == material_id)
.first()` and never compare material.user_id to the caller (routes_study_tools.py:102,174,300).
review_card writes a StudyCardState row for the caller against the foreign material_id
(routes_study_tools.py:122-140); get_deck_mastery can infer another user's deck size and state counts
(321-331); grade_quiz reads the foreign deck's content and answer keys (178-219).
evidence: server/routes_study_tools.py:43-54 - list endpoint correctly filters by user_id/shared_with
server/routes_study_tools.py:102 - m = db.query(StudyMaterial).filter(StudyMaterial.id == material_id).first() (no owner filter) in review_card
server/routes_study_tools.py:174 - same pattern in grade_quiz
server/routes_study_tools.py:300 - same pattern in get_deck_mastery
server/routes_study_tools.py:122-140 - writes StudyCardState for the caller's user_id against material_id
server/database.py:286 - unique key (user_id, material_id, card_index) is shared across users
findings.impact: Cross-account content and answer-key disclosure, plus the ability to poison another user's card states. Attack cost is one authenticated request with a guessed integer id.

findings.title: Second Canvas sync route bypasses SSRF validation while carrying the student's Bearer token
findings.symptom: POST /api/study/canvas/sync accepts an arbitrary canvas_url and sends the student's Canvas API token to it, following redirects.
findings.root_cause:
routes_study_tools.sync_canvas_lms builds the base URL from the request body with
only an http/https prefix check and calls httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=35,
headers={Authorization: Bearer <token>}, follow_redirects=True) (routes_study_tools.py:384-394). The
project already has the correct guard, ssrf.validate_safe_url (ssrf.py:98-111) with a redirect hook
(ssrf.py:104-111), and the other Canvas engine calls it (canvas_sync.py:26). This route omits it. The
token is not persisted but is exfiltratable in transit.
evidence: server/routes_study_tools.py:384-394 - user-supplied base_url used verbatim; Bearer token in headers; follow_redirects=True; no validate_safe_url
server/canvas_sync.py:26 - the other engine does validate_safe_url(self.base_url)
server/ssrf.py:98-111 - validate_safe_url / check_redirect_ssrf available but unused by this route
server/tests/test_canvas_sync.py:86-96 - the route is tested only with a mocked httpx client at a benign host
server/tests/test_security_hardened.py:66-72 - SSRF rejection is tested for CanvasSyncEngine only
server/main.py:423-448 - a second, guarded Canvas implementation (/api/canvas/test, /api/canvas/sync) via CanvasSyncEngine
findings.impact: Theft of a student's long-lived LMS token (full account API access) and an SSRF primitive from the public host, plus two divergent Canvas implementations that will drift.

findings.title: 'Tutor savings' ROI is fabricated arithmetic over client-supplied study time
findings.symptom: The dashboard shows a money-saved figure (study_hours * $50 - monthly_cost) presented as return on the subscription.
findings.root_cause:
calculate_value_metrics hardcodes plan costs {basic:10, pro:20, elite:40} and a
$50/hour tutor rate and derives study_hours from StudySession.time_spent_minutes (analytics.py:114-133).
That time is client-supplied: review defaults to 1 minute per card (routes_study_tools.py:24,151) and
quiz to 5 (routes_study_tools.py:34,228) with no server-side validation or timing.
evidence: server/analytics.py:119-126 - hardcoded plan_costs and `tutor_savings = study_hours * 50 - cost`
server/analytics.py:116-117 - study_hours summed from StudySession.time_spent_minutes
server/routes_study_tools.py:24,151 - review time defaults to 1 minute per card, client-supplied
server/routes_study_tools.py:34,228 - quiz time defaults to 5, client-supplied
server/analytics.py:136-144 - module history: compute_next_best_action was already rewritten to stop returning invented recommendations
findings.impact: A billing-adjacent claim that is effectively fabricated and gameable by posting a large time_spent_minutes.

Change line 209 to:

fixes.change:
Make the shipped behaviour match the published policy. Three mechanical edits:
1) draft.py: add an integrity clause to both build_style_prompt (line 76-91) and build_default_style_prompt (line 100-118): 'Do not submit this draft as your own work. It is a revision scaffold: cite only sources the student supplied, never invent a citation, and mark every unattributed claim. Begin the output with the line: "AI-GENERATED DRAFT - NOT FOR SUBMISSION (Helpotron)."'
2) launch_to_doc.py:79-87: flip TYPING_DEFAULTS["trusted_keys"] to False so keystrokes are ordinary DOM events (isTrusted:false) unless the user explicitly opts in, and change the comment's stated rationale from detector evasion to accessibility. Keep the cadence presets but document them as assistive-typing pacing, not authorship simulation.
3) PRIVACY_POLICY.md:87: either delete the 'transparency risk meter, not a concealing tool' sentence or make it true by removing the retry-until-detectors-pass loop (draft.py:225-293) and the 'is_stealth_ready' verdict (humanizer.py:567). Recommended: keep the sentence and make the code honest.
If the owner deliberately wants the evasion product, then this finding is a knowing risk acceptance - but the policy text must stop claiming the opposite.
fixes.risk: This is a product-positioning change, not a bug fix. Flipping trusted_keys may break typing on sites that reject synthetic events; the opt-in switch preserves that. Removing the detector-retry loop raises average detector scores and will surface more 'risky' drafts to users who relied on it. All three are reversible config/prompt changes.
fixes.verify: Grep proves the intent strings are gone: `rg -n 'detection evasion|eliminate all statistical AI markers|trusted_keys.: True' server/` -> 0 hits for the evasion phrasing. Then generate one draft through POST /api/drafts and assert the returned text starts with 'AI-GENERATED DRAFT - NOT FOR SUBMISSION'. Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest server/tests/ -q` and compare to the recorded baseline.

fixes.change:
Ground every generator in the student's source. In _SYSTEM (36-43) add: 'Every claim in your output must be traceable to the supplied transcript. For each flashcard, quiz question and study-guide bullet, include a "source" field containing a verbatim span of at most 25 words copied from the transcript. If the transcript does not contain the answer, omit the item and add it to a top-level "not_covered" list instead of guessing.'
Change the JSON contracts: flashcards become {"q","a","source"}; practice-test MC items gain "source" and "answer_index"; study guide and summary must end each section with a 'From the transcript:' quote. In generate_flashcards (129-144) and generate_practice_test (169-178) reject parsed items lacking a non-empty "source" and retry once. Add a `difficulty: str = "medium"` parameter to generate_flashcards/generate_practice_test that scales distractor similarity and Bloom level, wired from the existing client `difficulty` selector (web/src/components/study/MasteryRing.jsx:82-98) instead of the currently cosmetic field.
fixes.risk: Output length grows and strict source validation can exhaust the 2-attempt retry budget on poor transcripts (the honest outcome is an item being dropped, which is intended). Distractor difficulty changes may alter existing tests that assert item shape. Transcripts that are images-only will now legitimately produce sparse decks.
fixes.verify: Add a unit test feeding a short transcript and asserting every returned flashcard has a non-empty source span that is a substring of the transcript, and feeding an unrelated transcript asserting items land in not_covered rather than being invented. Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest server/tests/test_study_tools_v3.py -q`.

external_research.what: Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler (FSRS) - the algorithm helpotron claims to implement; reference implementations and parameters
external_research.why: Gives the canonical DSR transitions and the persisted-state contract Helpotron is missing (stability, difficulty, elapsed days, desired retention). Adopting it as the specification for H9-X3 makes the scheduler testable against a known oracle.

external_research.what: FSRS4Anki tutorial + Anki FAQ on which algorithm Anki uses
external_research.why: Documents that FSRS state must be carried per card across reviews and that user-tunable retention is the only knob; confirms that calling it stateless is not an implementation of FSRS at all.

external_research.what: Anki FAQ - what spaced repetition algorithm does Anki use
external_research.why: Independent statement of the SM-2 -> FSRS transition and why Anki made FSRS the default for new decks; useful as the neutral reference in the report.

The classic baseline: fixed ease factor + interval, reset to 1 day on a lapse. Even SM-2 persists per-card EF and interval - more than Helpotron does. Establishes that the current route is below even the 1987 algorithm.
external_research.verdict: reject+because inferior to FSRS for long-term retention, but it is the correct floor to benchmark against

external_research.what: Retrieval practice / distributed practice efficacy meta-analysis (Donoghue & Hattie 2021)
external_research.why: Practice testing d=0.74 and distributed practice d=0.85 across 242 studies - the exact two techniques Helpotron's UI invokes. Grounds the claim that a constant-interval deck and a 100%-always quiz deliver none of the benefit they advertise.

external_research.what: Kestin & Miller et al., 'AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning' (Nature Scientific Reports 2025; Research Square preprint 2024)
external_research.why: The strongest RCT evidence for AI tutors: effect size ~0.63-1.3 SD. Crucially the paper attributes the gain to expert-authored solution content, one-step-at-a-time scaffolding and accuracy guardrails - the opposite of Helpotron's answer-emission and ungrounded generation. Defines what a real AI study tool must do.

external_research.what: Harvard Gazette coverage of the PS2 AI-tutor study
external_research.why: Plain-language corroboration of the design-centred framing (scaffolds, not answers) for the report's value test.

external_research.what: University of Exeter academic honesty guidance on GenAI use (2025-26)
external_research.why: Representative tiered policy: AI-assisted use is permitted only with prompt/output logging and disclosure; 'using AI may not be cheating - but hiding it could be a breach of academic integrity'. Helpotron has no disclosure mechanism and actively hides, which is the exposure.

external_research.what: Langara College EdTech, 'Accuracy of Turnitin's AI Detection' (Sept 2025)
external_research.why: Measured evidence that humanizer/paraphraser tools drive AI-generated text to 0% detected, including after Turnitin's Aug 2025 update. Shows the Helpotron humanizer loop is both effective at concealment and that detector scores are not integrity evidence.
Institutional pushback showing detection is losing legitimacy as an enforcement mechanism - so a study tool's integrity value must come from scaffolding and disclosure, not from detector evasion.
